concepts.name: Flue-pipe voicing by hand (cutup, flueway, toe adjustment for timbre/volume/attack)
concepts.open_problem: Each flue pipe must be hand-adjusted (cutup height, flueway depth, toe diameter) to achieve target tone, volume and attack; the right result is judged by ear pipe-by-pipe and is not reducible to a formula. Whether a target timbre can be reached is discovered only empirically per pipe.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - voicing is performed one pipe at a time by a specialist voicer on bespoke, one-off instruments; there is no mass-production line that voices flue pipes by formula
concepts.app_market_check: 'organ pipe voicing app' - none seen (only tuning apps like Organ Tuner exist; no voicing-decision app)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Voicing of a pipe organ is the art of achieving the required tonal quality from each pipe, as distinct from tuning (setting its pitch or frequency).

concepts.name: Voicing as un-codifiable hand skill (tacit knowledge transfer problem)
concepts.open_problem: The voicer's judgment of when a pipe 'sounds right' is tacit and resists explicit codification; experts say it cannot be written down or transferred by instruction, which blocks both automation and apprenticeship scale-up.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - relies on individual artistic judgment per bespoke instrument; nothing in industry captures or reproduces this tacit decision step
concepts.app_market_check: 'voicing skill / tacit voicing assistant app' - none seen
concepts.verbatim_quote: It's all in the hand skills...You cannot write a book about that.

concepts.name: Pipe speech / attack transient control (nicking the languid, chiff)
concepts.open_problem: Controlling a pipe's onset transient ('chiff'/speech) via languid nicking and jet-lip geometry to get a clean, repeatable attack without mode-switching is done by feel; the mapping from physical tweak to perceived speech is not predictively solved per pipe.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - academic acoustics studies model attack transients (e.g. BME thesis, IOA paper), but the actual nicking decisions on real pipes remain manual and non-industrial
concepts.app_market_check: 'organ pipe speech / chiff tuning app' - none seen
concepts.verbatim_quote: Nicking of the languid, and sometimes labium, dampens the attack transients, reduces noise from air flow around the mouth and prevents random mode switching.

concepts.name: Articulateness / consonant-tone tradeoff in voicing a whole organ
concepts.open_problem: Achieving an articulate ('speaking') organ without sacrificing good tone, across a whole instrument and a specific room acoustic, remains a stated unsolved problem for the organ builder, dependent on architecture and judgment rather than a known procedure.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - framed as a per-room, per-instrument builder's problem; no industrial process targets articulateness
concepts.verbatim_quote: An organ should be articulate above everything else.

concepts.name: Free-reed (harmonium/reed-organ) tuning by filing the reed tongue
concepts.open_problem: Each free reed is tuned to pitch by scraping/filing metal from the tongue (tip = flat, base = sharp); over-removal is irreversible, so the amount to remove per reed is a fine manual judgment, and voicing for timbre across many reeds compounds it.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - factory reed instruments (accordions/harmoniums) are made at scale, but final fine tuning/voicing of individual reeds is still done by hand filing, not an automated industrial step
concepts.app_market_check: 'harmonium reed tuning app' - none seen (general tuner apps only)
concepts.verbatim_quote: Harmonium reeds are tuned by filing or scraping metal off one side of the vibrating tongue of the reed—one side makes it sharp, the other makes it flat.

concepts.name: Plate graduation: carving thickness map to the individual wood
concepts.open_problem: The thickness graduation (varying plate thickness across top/back) must be tailored to each unique billet of wood; the optimal map is not known until the finished instrument is played, so makers rely on past plans and iterate by intuition ('conversation with the wood').
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - factory/mass-produced violins make 'perfect copies' that are NOT tuned to the individual wood; the per-wood graduation decision is skipped industrially
concepts.app_market_check: 'violin plate graduation app' - none seen (research ML exists but no maker-facing app for graduation decisions)
concepts.verbatim_quote: The artistry of plate graduation remains deeply rooted in human experience, and no machine can yet replicate the nuanced decision-making of a seasoned luthier.

concepts.name: Tap-tone tuning (judging mode 2/5 frequencies by tapping the free plate)
concepts.open_problem: Makers tap the free plate and judge resonant 'tap-tones' (modes 2 and 5) plus mass to infer cross- and along-grain stiffness, then remove wood to hit targets; target frequencies disagree between authorities and the perceptual judgment of a 'good' tap-tone is tacit.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: no - mass-production violins are explicitly described as made with 'no master's hand', i.e. not tap-tone-tuned; power planing even destroys tap-tones, so industry does not perform this step
concepts.app_market_check: 'tap tone tuning app' - none seen as a graduation-decision tool (spectrum/tuner utilities only)
concepts.verbatim_quote: The frequencies of modes 2 and 5, informally known as 'tap-tones', in combination with the plate's mass, give an indication of the plate's stiffness across and along the grain respectively.

concepts.name: Chladni free-plate mode tuning (sand-pattern node visualization)
concepts.open_problem: Luthiers excite the free plate and read Chladni sand patterns to see mode shapes, then shave wood to make patterns/symmetry match a target; relating these node patterns to final tone of the assembled violin is still partly empirical.
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - Chladni/modal methods (Hutchins/Schleske) and recent ML eigenfrequency prediction exist in research/high-end studios, but this is not a standardized industrial production process
concepts.app_market_check: 'Chladni plate tuning app' - none seen as a luthier decision app
concepts.verbatim_quote: Chladni patterns show the geometry of the different types of vibration of violin plates.

concepts.name: ML prediction of carved-plate eigenfrequencies (the encroaching AI front)
concepts.open_problem: Recorded as a counter-case: a neural network now predicts a top plate's first ten free eigenfrequencies from geometry/mechanics, letting makers match two violins from different woods. This narrows but does not close the gap (it predicts modes, not the tacit shaving decisions or final played tone).
concepts.has_industrial_analog: partial - this is research/luthier-facing AI (Politecnico di Milano) and a niche app, not an industrial-scale analog; it shows domain B is NOT pure white space
concepts.app_market_check: 'violin plate AI / Violin Intelligence app' - SEEN (authentication/analysis app exists; eigenfrequency NN is research-stage)
concepts.verbatim_quote: The neural network receives as input the geometrical and mechanical parameters that define a violin top plate and outputs its first ten eigenfrequencies computed in free boundary conditions.

notes: HONEST FINDINGS (R5, only what I actually saw). NO-INDUSTRIAL-ANALOG + ZERO/near-zero-AI concepts (strongest v2 white space): (1) Flue-pipe voicing by hand (very-low AI, no analog - bespoke one-off instruments, only tuning apps exist); (2) Voicing as un-codifiable tacit hand skill (zero AI, no analog - 'You cannot write a book about that'); (3) Articulateness/tone tradeoff per room (zero AI, no analog); (4) Free-reed filing tuning (zero AI, partial analog - factories make reeds but final filing is manual); (5) Plate graduation to the individual wood (low AI, NO industrial analog - factory violins are 'perfect copies' not tuned to the wood); (6) Tap-tone tuning (very-low AI, NO analog - mass-production explicitly skips it, power planing destroys tap-tones). DISCRIMINATOR NUANCE per the run brief: factory violins exist but do NOT graduate plates by tap-tone - confirmed by source stating mass-produced violins are made 'with no master's hand ever touching them'; so tap-tone/graduation is genuinely no-industrial-analog. COUNTER-CASE that breaks pure white space: domain B has an encroaching AI front - Politecnico di Milano neural network predicts carved-plate eigenfrequencies (~98% accuracy) and a 'Violin Intelligence' app exists, plus AI-design-assist claims for organ building (organworks.com) and accelerometer-based automatic reed-pipe tuning devices (US patent 11626089). These are research/bespoke/niche, NOT industrial analogs, but they mean ai_penetration is moderate for the eigenfrequency-prediction concept and low for Chladni modal tuning - the tacit shaving/voicing DECISION steps remain the untouched white space, not the physics prediction. Organ side has the cleanest white space: voicing decisions (timbre, attack/chiff, articulateness) show no app and no industrial analog. Wikipedia note: Voicing_(pipe_organ) and Pipe_organ_tuning are real WP pages; Chladni/free-plate detail came mostly from UNSW/Strad/Guild-of-American-Luthiers rather than WP.
